key_insight: Across 2.08 million hospital encounters, more complex early warning models offered only small average gains over NEWS, with most benefit concentrated in patients already flagged as high risk.
clinical_relevance: A simpler approach may be sufficient for many low-risk encounters, while higher-risk patients may warrant fuller scoring or more advanced prediction tools.
method: Multi-centre retrospective cohort across 15 Danish hospitals (2018–2023)
Compared NEWS with simplified NEWS, DEWS, and an XGBoost-based model using vitals, demographics, labs, and history embeddings
Used propensity score weighting to address intervention bias and assessed net benefit, AUC, and calibration
evidence_signal: Decision-curve analysis found very small overall net-benefit differences, but much larger gains in the high-risk subgroup (initial NEWS ≥7).
watch_item: Because the study is retrospective, performance may be affected by residual confounding and the findings need prospective validation before changing triage workflows.
paper_title: Development and validation of early warning scores predicting 24-hour mortality addressing intercurrent medical interventions: a multi-centre retrospective cohort study of 2,08 million hospital encounters
